title: Incomplete Conquest
summary: After Joshua's death Judah, with Simeon, goes up first against the Canaanites and takes Jerusalem and Hebron; Othniel wins Caleb's daughter Achsah by taking Debir. But Judah cannot drive out those with iron chariots, and Benjamin, Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, Naphtali and Dan all fail to clear the Canaanites. The angel of the LORD comes up from Gilgal to Bochim and tells Israel that, because they made covenants with the people of the land, God will not drive them out, and the people weep.

title: The Cycle of the Judges
summary: After Joshua's generation dies, a new generation that did not know the LORD serves the Baals and other gods. The LORD gives Israel into the hands of raiders, then raises up judges who deliver them, but when each judge dies the people return to worse ways. God leaves some nations in the land to test Israel and to teach war to a new generation, among them the Philistines, Canaanites, Sidonians and Hivites, and the Israelites live among them and intermarry.

title: Othniel, Ehud and Shamgar
summary: Israel serves the Baals, and the LORD gives them to Cushan-rishathaim for eight years until Othniel, a kinsman of Caleb, delivers them. Later Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, brings tribute to Eglon, king of Moab, kills him with a hidden dagger in his upper room, and rallies Israel to defeat Moab, bringing eighty years of rest. Shamgar son of Anath strikes down 600 Philistines with an ox goad.

title: Deborah and Barak
summary: Oppressed by Jabin of Canaan and his commander Sisera, who has nine hundred iron chariots, Israel cries out to the LORD. The prophetess Deborah summons Barak, who agrees to go only if she goes with him, and she says the honor will go to a woman. The LORD routs Sisera's army at the Kishon, and Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael, who gives him milk, covers him, and kills him with a tent peg. Deborah and Barak sing a victory song.

title: Gideon and the Midianites
summary: Midian oppresses Israel for seven years. The angel of the LORD calls Gideon, who is threshing wheat in a winepress, and Gideon tears down his father's Baal altar by night and tests God with a fleece. God reduces his army to three hundred; they surround the Midianite camp with trumpets and torches in jars, and the enemy flees. Gideon pursues the Midianite kings, refuses to rule over Israel, and makes an ephod that becomes a snare.

title: Abimelech
summary: After Gideon dies, his son Abimelech persuades Shechem to back him and kills seventy of his brothers on one stone; Jotham, the youngest, escapes and tells a fable of trees choosing a bramble as king. After three years God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem. Abimelech destroys the city and burns its tower, then is struck on the head by a millstone thrown by a woman at Thebez and has his armor-bearer kill him.

title: Jephthah's Vow
summary: Israel again serves foreign gods and is oppressed by the Philistines and Ammonites. The elders of Gilead bring back Jephthah, an outcast, as commander. He vows to offer whatever first comes from his house if he wins, defeats Ammon, and his only daughter comes out to meet him with dancing. She asks two months to mourn before the vow is carried out; what was done to her is debated. Jephthah later fights Ephraim and uses 'Shibboleth' to identify fugitives at the Jordan.

title: Samson
summary: An angel tells the barren wife of Manoah she will bear a Nazirite son who will begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines. Samson grows up, marries a Philistine woman at Timnah, kills a lion barehanded, and poses a riddle at the wedding. He burns the Philistines' grain with torch-bearing foxes and kills a thousand men with a jawbone. Delilah learns the secret of his strength, his hair is cut, and he is blinded; he pulls down the temple of Dagon at Gaza, dying with many Philistines.

title: Micah's Idols and the Danites
summary: Micah of Ephraim takes silver from his mother, returns it, and she has some made into an idol; he sets up a household shrine and hires a young Levite from Bethlehem as his priest. The tribe of Dan, seeking land, sends five spies who stay at Micah's house. Six hundred Danites take the idol and the priest, who goes willingly, then attack the quiet and peaceful town of Laish, burn it, and rename it Dan.

title: The Levite and Gibeah
summary: A Levite from Ephraim's hill country fetches his concubine from Bethlehem and on the return stops at Gibeah of Benjamin. An old man shelters him, but men of the town demand the Levite, and the concubine is given to them and abused through the night; she dies at the door. The Levite divides her body and sends the pieces to the tribes, and Israel goes to war and nearly wipes out Benjamin. The tribes then find wives for the survivors from Jabesh-gilead and Shiloh.
